diagnostic_instrument: M.I.N.I. PLUS (Norwegian version, modules A, C, D, K, L, M); DSM-IV broad schizophrenia spectrum disorder
diagnosis_confirmed: diagnostic interview at baseline by clinicians trained in the instrument
overlap_notes: Five reports on one cohort of 148 starters. evensen2017 and gjerdalen2023 report the whole 148; evensen2019 the 69 who consented to register extraction; lystad2017 and klungsyr2021 the 131 who completed neurocognitive assessment. Six counties, three randomised to CR and three to CBT; no non-augmented control arm existed ('A control group without the augmentation proved impossible to include', klungsyr2021, Sample, p. 3). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01139502.
employment_selection_verbatim: RECRUITMENT INTO A VOCATIONAL SERVICE: 'Participants were recruited from local mental health centres and vocational services within the six catchment areas. Self-referral was also possible.' (evensen2017, Participants, p. 181); 'Participants were recruited from within the mental health services, NAV, and through self-referral in the six counties that were involved in the JUMP study.' (evensen2019, Participants, p. 2; NAV is the Norwegian Labour and Welfare Administration). | COHORT MEMBERSHIP REQUIRED STARTING THE VOCATIONAL REHABILITATION: 'A total of 319 persons were referred to the JUMP study. Of these, 76 did not meet the inclusion criteria and 61 declined, mainly due to lack of motivation, poor timing, or reluctance to participate in research. Another nine did not complete the assessments, and 25 did not start the vocational rehabilitation after assessment. The remaining 148 participants were included in the study between August 2009 and March 2012' (evensen2017, p. 182); Figure 1 prints '173 Eligible / 25 non-starters' feeding '148 starters' (p. 182). | WORK MOTIVATION ASSERTED OF THE WHOLE SAMPLE: 'In this study, where all the participants exhibited some level of motivation to work, those with the best requirements, showed the highest probability of obtaining employment.' (gjerdalen2023, Discussion, p. 28). | NOT baseline unemployment: the listed inclusion criteria are 'age between 18-65 years, an IQ above 70, a diagnosis within the [DSM-IV] criteria for a broad schizophrenia spectrum disorder, and adequate understanding of the Norwegian language' (evensen2017, p. 182) and contain no employment condition, and 'At the start of the intervention all participants were reliant on social security benefits, and 17% had some form of employment' (evensen2017, Background, p. 181), so being wholly out of work was not required.
